description: Start a Strategy Lab optimization run on one of your own strategies: an AI mutation loop that repeatedly tweaks the strategy code, backtests each variant, and keeps improvements (walk-forward validated: trains on trainSplit of the window, validates on the rest). This is different from generate_strategy -- that writes one strategy from a description; this iteratively improves an EXISTING strategy you already own. Does not create new strategies. Wallet-charging: call once WITHOUT acknowledgeCost to get a cost estimate (no charge, nothing queued), confirm the spend with the user, then call again with acknowledgeCost:true to actually start. Requires the mcp:live OAuth scope. Only one run can be active per user at a time. When the run finishes, its best version is checked out of sample (on the part of the window it was not trained on). The best version becomes the strategy's latestVersion ONLY if it passes that check (single-pair runs: also when the check is inconclusive, e.g. too few out-of-sample trades). Otherwise -- it failed the check, or the run was cancelled -- the version is HELD: latestVersion and the bots following it are not changed, and get_optimization_status shows progress.verdict, progress.heldBecause and progress.heldVersionId (savedVersionId is absent). The strategy author can still accept a held version in the TradeStaq web app ("Use this version anyway"). Promoted to stable automatically ONLY if autoPromote:true AND the result clears a strict bar (see autoPromote param); otherwise use promote_strategy_version yourself once you like the result. MULTI-PAIR (basket) RUNS: pass symbols (primary first) to test every candidate on several pairs of the same exchange account and market type, so the result is not tuned to one chart. Pricing is the base per experiment plus an extra charge per extra pair per experiment, billed per pair actually evaluated. A multi-pair request always returns a cost_estimate first with a quoteId, the pairs, the maximum cost and estimatedMinutes; the quote is a maximum, and a run time limit may cut experiments (clampedFrom, expectedExperimentsWithinBudget). Confirm by calling again with the same arguments plus acknowledgeCost:true and that quoteId (or acknowledgedCost). If the response has quoteChanged:true, show the new estimate and confirm again with its new quoteId. A multi-pair run passes only if the best version beats the original on most pairs, wrecks no pair, and loses money out of sample on no pair; otherwise it is held (an inconclusive check also holds a multi-pair run), and get_optimization_status shows the per-pair results.

acknowledgeCost.description: Set true only after showing the user the estimated cost (from a prior call without this flag, or from check_auth's wallet balance) and getting their approval. False (default) returns a cost preview and starts nothing.

acknowledgedCost.description: Multi-pair runs only: the estimatedCost the user approved. Used when the quote has expired: the run starts if the fresh price is not above it, otherwise a new estimate comes back (quoteChanged:true).

autoPromote.description: If true, automatically promote the run's final saved version to the stable channel (what every bot on that strategy actually runs) when the run completes -- skipping the separate promote_strategy_version step. Only takes effect if the run found a real improvement AND the out-of-sample check returned a passing verdict (an inconclusive or failed check never auto-promotes) AND the result is profitable out of sample AND it is no worse out of sample than the current stable version; otherwise nothing is promoted (the version is handled exactly like a normal run: latestVersion on a pass, held otherwise), and get_optimization_status.progress.autoPromoteSkippedReason explains why. Confirm with the user before setting this true -- it changes what live bots run without a separate review step, the same way promote_strategy_version does. Default false preserves the old behavior (never auto-promotes).

endDate.description: ISO date for the end of the backtest window. Defaults to now.

exchangeId.description: An exchange you own (paper or live), from list_exchanges. Used only to source historical candle data.

maxExperiments.description: How many mutate-and-backtest experiments to run (1-30). Cost scales linearly with this -- fewer experiments for a quick/cheap check, more for a thorough search.

presetProfiles.description: Which risk profiles the preset search should cover. Omit for all four. Cost scales per profile, so naming one or two is the cheaper option when the user only cares about a particular risk shape. Ignored unless searchPresets is true.

quoteId.description: Multi-pair runs only: the quoteId from the cost_estimate the user approved. Send it with acknowledgeCost:true and the same other arguments; the run then uses exactly that quote.

scoringProfile.description: balanced: Performance-first: return drives the score, quality (Sharpe x profit factor) and win rate add, drawdown penalizes. | conservative: Low drawdown + consistent returns, scaled so a lucky handful of low-risk trades cannot win over a larger sample. | aggressive: Maximize total return -- return is the dominant factor, profit factor capped to prevent cherry-picking. | consistency: High win rate + Sortino ratio with a strict minimum trade count -- must trade frequently and win consistently.

searchPresets.description: Also search for per-risk-profile PARAMETER PRESETS once the code-mutation loop finishes -- tuning the strategy's own knobs separately for each risk profile, then walk-forward validating each winner and publishing the ones that clear the bar. Charged SEPARATELY and per profile on top of the experiment cost, so the estimate returned without acknowledgeCost breaks it out under presetSearch -- show that to the user before confirming. Only runs if the mutation loop actually found an improvement. Requires an admin to have priced it; the request is refused with a clear message if not. On a multi-pair run every candidate is tested on every pair, so each profile costs the per-profile price plus an extra charge per extra pair (shown under presetSearch and costBreakdown.presetSearch in the quoteId estimate), it adds to estimatedMinutes, and it is billed only if the search finishes; until an admin prices the multi-pair search it is refused with code preset_search_single_pair_only.

startDate.description: ISO date for the start of the backtest window. Defaults to 6 months ago.

strategyId.description: ID of your own strategy to optimize, from list_strategies(owned:true) or get_strategy.

symbol.description: Trading pair to optimize against. Defaults to BTC/USDT when symbols is not given. With symbols, it only picks which listed pair is the primary and must be one of symbols (any case); a symbol that is not in symbols is refused with code symbol_not_in_symbols and nothing is quoted. Prefer omitting it and listing the primary first in symbols.

symbols.description: Pairs to test on, primary first, all on the same exchange account and market type, e.g. ["BTC/USDT","ETH/USDT","SOL/USDT"]. Entries are trimmed, empty ones dropped and duplicates (any case) removed; a list that comes down to one pair is a plain single-pair run. More than one pair tests every candidate on every pair (a multi-pair run, priced per extra pair per experiment and confirmed with quoteId). Capped by the user's plan (Free 1 / Pro 3 / Trader 4 / Whale 5) and by the system cap (5 by default, never above 8), and only available when the server has multi-pair runs on; a request over the cap is refused with code too_many_assets, maxAssets and an upgrade hint. Combinable with searchPresets only once an admin has priced the multi-pair preset search (otherwise refused with code preset_search_single_pair_only): every preset candidate is then tested on every pair. Omit for a single-pair run.

trainSplit.description: Fraction of the window used for training vs. out-of-sample validation (0.5-0.9).

userGuidance.description: Free-text steering for the AI mutations, e.g. "focus on reducing drawdown" (max 2000 chars).

name: start_optimization_run
